name: Jason Horne-Francis
summary: Rated the most complete prospect of the crop: a powerful, explosive midfielder-forward who was already a consistent SANFL League player at 17–18, won it at the coalface and marked strongly forward. Best on ground in the preliminary final. Kicking consistency and outside game were the only knocks.

name: Sam Darcy
summary: Fast-developing 204cm tall after a big growth spurt who could play either key post, with athleticism, clean hands and great reach in the air. Western Bulldogs father-son. Needed to add a lot of strength.

name: Finn Callaghan
summary: Prototype tall, athletic midfielder with a long, penetrating left foot and slick evasion, compared to Josh Kelly and Bontempelli. Moved to an inside role in his draft year and his numbers jumped. Contested work was the main thing to build.

name: Nick Daicos
summary: Collingwood father-son who dominated every game: an elite reader of the play who always knew where the next possession was coming from, averaging 36 disposals and 2 goals (136 fantasy) for Oakleigh. Captained the AFL Academy. Strength and impact per kick were the only questions.

name: Mac Andrew
summary: Melbourne academy ruck-forward with ridiculous athleticism and leap, but a very light frame and raw game. Pure upside pick, rated for what he could become rather than what he was producing.

name: Josh Rachele
summary: Mercurial small forward compared to Toby Greene, with a soccer background, quick feet, great skills and a keen eye for goal; the best small forward in his crop. Consistency and defensive work rate were the knocks.

name: Josh Ward
summary: Big riser in his draft year: a classy, durable centre-bounce midfielder who won mountains of the ball (30 disposals, 101 fantasy) with clean skills; Vic Metro captain and Talent League Team of the Year captain. Viewed as a safe, high-floor pick. Athleticism was the only real knock.

name: Jye Amiss
summary: Deadeye leading key forward who kicked 51 goals in the WAFL Colts and was rarely held to fewer than two. Gets separation on the lead with ease. Contested marking and impact away from goal were the work-ons; a late knee injury was a flag.

name: Josh Gibcus
summary: The standout key defender of the crop: an athletic, springy intercept marker with sticky hands who can also set up attacks. Kicking and ball-winning volume were the work-ons.

name: Neil Erasmus
summary: Prolific, tall goalkicking midfielder who also marks strongly forward and has a good engine; seen as AFL-ready as a forward first. Kicking consistency and explosive speed were the knocks.

name: Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera
summary: Classy wingman with elite pedigree who used the ball as well as anyone in his draft, with composure and evasion; rated SA's second-best prospect. Strength and inside game were the work-ons.

name: Josh Sinn
summary: Line-breaking half-back moving into the midfield, with speed and a big kick. Slid from a top-10 tip after an interrupted year. Kicking consistency and composure were the work-ons.

name: Ben Hobbs
summary: The best pure inside midfielder in the draft: hard-nosed, consistent, wins clearances and tackles hard. Outside game and kicking were the work-ons.

name: Campbell Chesser
summary: Speedy, classy outside runner who breaks lines from half-back or the wing. Injury and lockdowns limited him to a handful of games. Contested ball and tackling were the work-ons.

name: Leek Aleer
summary: Mature-age, athletically gifted tall defender with a big leap and eye-catching intercept marking, but still raw and inconsistent. Taken much earlier than projected.

name: Darcy Wilmot
summary: Tenacious, brave half-back who breaks lines with speed and run-and-carry, and leads with his voice. Midfield craft and composure were the work-ons.

name: Tom Brown
summary: Smooth-moving, smart half-back who reads the play and provides run and drive out of defence, with the option of a wing. Contested work and strength were the work-ons.

name: Angus Sheldrick
summary: Strong inside bull who bustles through congestion and wins the ball consistently through sheer will; reliable at every level he played. Kicking consistency and athleticism were the knocks.

name: Jacob van Rooyen
summary: Physically imposing key forward who can swing back, with a strong aerial presence and contested marking. Endurance and four-quarter output were the work-ons.

name: Kai Lohmann
summary: Elite athlete with speed, evasion and a big leap, dangerous in the air and at ground level as a medium forward. Low accumulator; off-ball work and finishing were the work-ons.

name: Matthew Johnson
summary: Tall, composed, slick-moving midfielder who was one of the most reliable users of the ball in the crop. Production and contested ball were the knocks.

name: Josh Goater
summary: One of the best athletes in the draft: an explosive 190cm midfielder who escapes congestion like no one else and marks well. Kicking and running capacity kept him out of top-five talk.

name: Sam Banks
summary: Tasmania's top prospect: a smooth-moving half-back with pinpoint kicking and good decisions who can roll into the midfield. Inside game and defensive pressure were the questions.

name: Judson Clarke
summary: One of the quickest players in the pool: a surging small forward and midfielder with goal sense and run-and-carry. Contested game and tackling were the work-ons.

name: Brady Hough
summary: One of the year's biggest bolters: a versatile, poised user of the ball who rose quickly into draft contention. Limited exposure and midfield craft were the questions.

name: James Willis
summary: Strongly built, powerful midfielder who can play multiple roles and put up big numbers (103 fantasy average in the SANFL under-18s). Finishing and kicking at speed were the work-ons.

name: Matthew Roberts
summary: Hard-working, high-IQ midfielder and half-forward who hits the scoreboard; a long-time standout SA junior who came back from a mid-year injury. Athleticism and composure were the knocks.

name: Paul Curtis
summary: Crafty small forward with X-factor who can win a game in a burst, dangerous both on the lead and at ground level (2 goals a game). Endurance, midfield craft and finishing consistency were the work-ons.

name: Jake Soligo
summary: Hard-working, agile ball winner who racks up the footy and tackles hard (89 fantasy average) and can pinch-hit forward. Kicking consistency and hurt factor were the knocks.

name: Rhett Bazzo
summary: Swingman who looks most at home in defence, reading the play, intercepting and using it well by foot. Consistency and repeat defensive efforts were the work-ons.

name: Miller Bergman
summary: Versatile outside mover with a penetrating kick and strong marking who can play half-back, wing or forward. Composure, strength and inside game were the work-ons.

name: Blake Howes
summary: Highly athletic forward with highlight-reel marks and the ability to play further afield. An upside pick; consistency and contested game were the work-ons.

name: Corey Warner
summary: Hard-running midfielder (brother of Chad) who plays inside and out and breaks forward with purpose and a long left foot. Kicking consistency and composure were the work-ons.

name: Toby Conway
summary: Strong, smart, hard-working ruck with a good endurance base who wins it around the ground and dominates stoppages. Athleticism, kicking and versatility were the work-ons.

name: Mitch Knevitt
summary: Big-bodied 193cm inside midfielder with power, endurance and a big leap who can also go forward. Tested very well. Composure and ground-level work were the work-ons.

name: Connor MacDonald
summary: Accumulating inside midfielder who had an outstanding Talent League year (30 disposals, 121 fantasy average) with stoppage craft, run and carry and defensive pressure. Kicking consistency and finishing were the work-ons.

name: Jesse Motlop
summary: Crafty, natural small forward who doesn't need much of the ball to hurt you, with great goal sense and flair; already had senior experience. Consistency, production and strength were the knocks.

name: Tyler Sonsie
summary: Stoppage specialist with the best two-sided kick in the draft and slick hands, who can also go forward and kick goals; rated top-five at his best. Consistency and gut running were the knocks.

name: James Tunstill
summary: Hard-working midfielder dangerous both in close and on the outside, who played his way into contention in the WA Colts and at state level. Kicking and four-quarter consistency were the work-ons.

name: Josh Fahey
summary: The leading northern academy prospect of 2021: a dashing half-back with a penetrating left foot and run-and-carry. Limited exposure and kicking consistency were the questions.

name: Arthur Jones
summary: Raw, athletic wingman with a rare speed-and-endurance mix and X-factor. Contested game, strength and limited exposure were the flags.

name: Zac Taylor
summary: Crafty small midfielder-forward with outstanding vision and decision-making who found plenty of the ball (26 disposals, 96 fantasy). Strength and inside game were the work-ons.

name: Arlo Draper
summary: Classy, agile midfielder-forward with stoppage craft and the ability to hit the scoreboard; a high-upside SA prospect averaging over 100 fantasy in the under-18s. Strength, consistency and defensive running were the work-ons.

name: Alastair Lord
summary: Quick, skilful and smart small midfielder-defender who accumulates and hurts with the ball. Contested work, strength and defensive side were the work-ons.

name: Marcus Windhager
summary: St Kilda academy riser: an explosive, powerful midfielder with clean hands and a turn of speed who can roll forward. Low accumulator; kicking consistency was the other work-on.

name: Cooper Murley
summary: Speedy, attacking midfielder who runs all day and uses it well, with the option of a forward role. Ankle and collarbone injuries wrecked his draft year and kept him out of first-round talk. Size and strength were the questions.

name: Oscar Adams
summary: Athletic 198cm tall who could play key defence or ruck. Production and consistency were the work-ons.

name: Harvey Harrison
summary: Hard-working inside midfielder who put up huge numbers in the SANFL under-18s (25 disposals, 5 clearances, 119 fantasy average). Kicking consistency and strength were the work-ons.

name: Jai Serong
summary: Skinny, high-upside tall who marks well and played in all three thirds of the ground. A long-term project; production and speed were the work-ons.

name: Eric 'Roy' Benning
summary: Fremantle academy ruck-forward who developed quickly, with athleticism, a big leap and a promising aerial game. Raw and inconsistent.

name: Hugh Jackson
summary: Natural accumulator who wins it inside and out and distributes well (29 disposals, 108 fantasy average in the SANFL under-18s). His form dipped late after a role change. Very left-foot dominant.

name: Dante Visentini
summary: Competitive, physical 201cm tall who can play on all three lines and in the ruck. Athleticism and production were the work-ons.

name: Jack Williams
summary: Versatile tall who marks well and kicks goals forward, and can rotate through the ruck or back. Speed and consistency were the knocks.

name: Lachlan Rankin
summary: Clever, efficient natural footballer who uses it well on all three lines. Strength and inside game were the work-ons.

name: Jackson Archer
summary: Accountable, competitive lockdown defender who wins his one-on-ones. Very little offensive output or production.

name: Jase Burgoyne
summary: Smooth mover who always seems to have time, rarely wastes a possession and accumulates heavily (29 disposals, 107 fantasy average). Projected as a half-back or wing. Kick penetration, contested game and strength were the work-ons.

name: Luke Cleary
summary: Over-age intercepting, rebounding defender with good positioning and efficient kicking. Contested game and hurt factor were the work-ons.

name: Cooper Whyte
summary: Hard, explosive stoppage midfielder with a penetrating kick and some flair. Accumulation and consistency were the work-ons.

name: Taj Woewodin
summary: Athletic, versatile Melbourne father-son prospect with a penetrating kick and good work rate. Kicking consistency and hurt factor were the work-ons.

name: Mitchito Owens
summary: One of the biggest improvers of his year: a fast-developing, explosive utility who runs both ways and takes gutsy marks. Consistency and limited exposure were the questions.

name: Sam Butler
summary: Clean, clever midfielder-forward with elite acceleration who is dangerous around goal and works hard defensively. Kicking consistency and decision-making were the work-ons.

name: Flynn Kroeger
summary: Rebounding defender from Eastern Ranges, picked late after a short 2021 Talent League season.

name: Garrett McDonagh
summary: Mature-age midfielder taken from Richmond’s VFL side at 25 after averaging 21 disposals and 86 fantasy points in 2021.

name: Greg Clark
summary: Mature-age inside midfielder from Subiaco: a 195cm ball-winner and tackler, with speed and upside the knocks on him.

name: Charlie Constable
summary: Second chance for the former Geelong top-20 pick: a big-bodied inside mid who averaged 33 disposals and 111 fantasy in the VFL in 2021.
